guide_line: Count unpaired electrons and name an orbital shape.
steps: An s orbital is a sphere. A p orbital is a dumbbell. There are three p orbitals in a shell.
One orbital holds at most two electrons, with opposite spins.
Hund’s rule: in one subshell, give every orbital one electron before any gets a pair.
Count the singles left in the last subshell. Those are the unpaired electrons.

worked_example.q: How many unpaired electrons does carbon have? Its last subshell is 2p2.
steps: Two electrons go in two different boxes.

similar_problem.q: How many unpaired electrons does nitrogen have? Its last subshell is 2p3.
similar_problem.hint: Three electrons and three p boxes.

problems.q: What is the shape of an s orbital?
problems.why: Every s orbital is a sphere.

problems.q: What is the shape of a p orbital?
problems.why: A p orbital has two lobes.
hints: There are three p orbitals, each a dumbbell.

problems.q: How many unpaired electrons does C have in its ground state?
problems.why: Fill the last subshell one electron per orbital before pairing.
hints: Do not pair electrons until every box in that subshell has one.
